question: Why did the error rate go up on 21 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of search v7.6 to ap-south may have introduced a new issue.
why_chain: The deployment of search v7.6 to ap-south caused a change in the error rate.
The error rate increased from 0.48% to 1.07% in service search in region ap-south.
The deployment of a new version (v7.6) to a new region (ap-south) is a plausible cause of the error rate increase.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume could have contributed to the error rate increase.
why_chain: The request volume increased by 23% in service search in region ap-south.
The error rate increased from 0.48% to 1.07% in service search in region ap-south.
The increase in request volume could have overwhelmed the system, leading to more errors.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increased after the deployment, not before or at the same time as the configuration change.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a dependency issue with an upstream service.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a dependency issue, as the error rate increased in the service itself and not in the upstream service.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a sudden increase in data quality.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of bad or unusual input data, as the error rate increased in the service itself and not in the input data.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a sudden increase in infrastructure capacity.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a sudden increase in infrastructure capacity, as the error rate increased in the service itself and not in the infrastructure.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service search in region ap-south rose from 0.48% to 1.07% (+122%), with a change point at 2026-03-21T11:55:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search in region ap-south: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.18).
At the same time, request volume for service search in region ap-south stayed about the same (511 per 5 min before, 627 per 5 min after, +23%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search in region ap-south stayed about the same (140 ms before, 138 ms after, -2%).
Deployed search v7.6 to ap-south (search, ap-south; 217 min before the change; record R009; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
search: WARN slow query 1.2s on report endpoint (single occurrence) (search, us-east; 94 min before the change; record R010; fit: describes a symptom, not a change)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 217 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✗ No logs or alerts from the affected segment confirm the problem.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Roll back the deployment of search v7.6 to ap-south to see if the error rate decreases.
Monitor the system for any further errors and request volume spikes, and take appropriate action if they occur.
Review the logs and metrics for any other services in the region that may have been affected by the deployment.
